text: **091. Logarithmic and Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequalities and the B-conjecture.** Proves the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures. For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout $`0\lt p\lt 1`$. ([Lean](lean/docs/091.md))
[The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture](preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)

We prove the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension. The theorem also gives the symmetric Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for every $`0\lt p\lt 1`$. Combined with Saroglou's transfer theorem and a support-subspace reduction, it yields the logarithmic inequality for every even log-concave Radon measure and the scalar-dilation $`(B)`$-conjecture.

Every prescribed-order finite sequence of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd has one signing for which every signed prefix has norm at most $`C\sqrt d`$, with C absolute and independent of the sequence length. Consequently, every indexed zero-sum family of unit-ball vectors admits an ordering with the same bound for its unsigned partial sums. This determines the Euclidean Steinitz constant up to absolute factors, $`S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)`$, and resolves the Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström conjecture.

**249. A finitely generated Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample.** Constructs a finitely generated residually finite group with integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture. It has no two-dimensional classifying space, even with infinitely many cells. ([Lean](lean/docs/249.md))
[A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture](preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)
We construct a finitely generated residually finite group of integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture.

We prove that the maximum number of mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in ℂ<sup>6</sup> is three, resolving Zauner's dimension-six MUB conjecture. The upper bound is computer-assisted: under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions, a complete execution of the documented verification pipeline excludes four arbitrary complex bases.

We prove a uniform positive spectral gap for the pure antiferromagnetic spin-one Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings, establishing the positive even-periodic formulation of the spin-one Haldane conjecture.

The [completed I46 report](iterations/i46-quantitative-logarithmic-stability.md) gives an **author-level proof** of P10: for arbitrary origin-symmetric planar convex bodies between fixed positive inner and outer balls, and interpolation parameters bounded away from zero and one, the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski deficit satisfies Δ ≥ c d𝓔^10. The distance is to the entire block-equality pair class, allowing unrestricted comparison bodies and oblique parallelograms. No smoothness, reflection, common fan, facet count or minimum facet mass is assumed. This positive partial requires independent proof and contribution review; it is not accepted as a seventh substantial finding or described as intrinsically enabled by the new all-dimensional corpus theorem.

E is the symmetric specialization of the mechanism in **Yude Liu, Qiang Sun, and Ge Xiong, *The centered logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality*, arXiv:2610.10152v2, 8 October 2026**, especially (3.10)–(3.16), Lemma 3.4, and §3.3. Full credit for that mechanism belongs there; neither I44 nor this audit claims discovery or priority. The external paper is **not an assumed theorem**. Its authors explicitly call it a proposed proof and state that their independent human verification is incomplete. This audit checks the symmetric reduction only; it does not certify their nonsymmetric theorem or replace that human verification.

* **E:** For every n≥2, full-dimensional origin-symmetric K,L⊂Rⁿ, and 0<λ<1, equality in logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski holds exactly when K=ΣKᵢ and L=ΣcᵢKᵢ on common nonzero complementary linear subspaces, cᵢ>0. The original subspaces need not be orthogonal.

**Van Handel**, *The local logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for zonoids*, [final author version `logzon221121.pdf`](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~rvan/logzon221121.pdf), Lemma 3.6 proves the planar Bochner bound by Cauchy–Schwarz and the explicit generating measure. Remark 3.4 displays the retained square rather than merely an inequality. Section 4, especially Lemmas 4.2–4.3, replaces the smooth eigenfunction equation by a nonsmooth mixed-area-measure identity; it is a real nonsmooth equality argument. The finite inverse sine operator below is a conjugate of this classical planar mixed-area structure. Rewriting it as a reversible Markov matrix is not, by itself, a new coercivity mechanism. The additional quantitative input used here is an existing graph theorem.

- [The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture](../../preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)

The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture asserts that logarithmic interpolation of origin-symmetric convex bodies preserves the geometric-mean lower bound for volume. The formalized result proves, for every dimension $n\ge1$, such bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$, and $0\le t\le1$, that their logarithmic Wulff combination has volume at least $|K|^{1-t}|L|^t$. It assumes neither boundary smoothness nor coordinatewise unconditionality.
